title: SaaS Admin Dashboard
problem: Needed a secure, production-grade authentication system without relying on third-party auth providers like Auth0 or Firebase Auth — full control over session management, token lifecycle, and security hardening.
architecture: Built a custom auth system with in-memory access tokens and httpOnly refresh token cookies. Added CSRF protection via double-submit cookie pattern, bcrypt password hashing with configurable salt rounds, a singleton initPromise guard to prevent race conditions during server bootstrap, and single-use refresh token rotation that invalidates tokens after each use to prevent replay attacks.
outcome: Production-ready auth flow with zero third-party auth dependency. Stateful refresh tokens stored in MongoDB enable immediate revocation on logout or compromise, with automatic token rotation on every refresh cycle.
keyEngineering: Custom JWT auth with httpOnly cookies, CSRF protection, single-use refresh token rotation, and race condition guards — no third-party auth providers.
lessons: Chose stateful refresh tokens over stateless JWT for revocation control — accepted the DB lookup cost on refresh as a worthwhile trade-off for security
Implemented single-use refresh token rotation to prevent token replay attacks
Built a singleton initPromise pattern to guard against race conditions during NestJS module initialization
Added CSRF double-submit cookie pattern to protect against cross-site request forgery on auth endpoints

title: TaskFlow — Task Management App
problem: Needed a full-stack Trello-like task management tool to demonstrate end-to-end monorepo architecture with a modern React frontend and NestJS API.
architecture: Monorepo with a NestJS REST API backend using Mongoose ODM for MongoDB, and a React 19 frontend built with Vite and Tailwind CSS v4. Complete CRUD operations for boards, lists, and cards with drag-and-drop reordering.
outcome: Fully functional task management app with monorepo architecture, clean API design, and a responsive Tailwind UI — demonstrating full-stack ownership from database schema to component design.
keyEngineering: Monorepo architecture with NestJS + React 19, Mongoose ODM, Tailwind v4, and Vite build pipeline.
lessons: Structured a monorepo with shared configuration across backend and frontend packages
Designed Mongoose schemas for nested board → list → card relationships with efficient querying
Implemented optimistic UI updates for card operations to keep the interface responsive
Used Tailwind CSS v4 with Vite for fast iteration on component styling

title: FinBot AI — Personal Finance Manager
problem: Users needed a zero-friction way to log expenses without leaving Telegram — including via voice messages in noisy environments.
architecture: Built a Node.js pipeline that chunks incoming Telegram audio, pipes it through Google Speech-to-Text, then runs a rule-based NLP categorizer before writing to a normalized PostgreSQL schema supporting multi-user isolation and monthly rollups.
outcome: Production bot handling voice + text input with automatic categorization, budget alerts, and monthly summaries — all stateless except for a lightweight session cache for multi-step flows.
keyEngineering: Chunked audio transcription pipeline → rule-based NLP categorizer → normalized PostgreSQL with per-user budget tracking.
lessons: Designed a chunked audio handling pipeline to stay within Speech-to-Text payload limits
Normalized a PostgreSQL schema for multi-user transaction isolation with efficient monthly aggregations
Built a rule-based NLP layer that degrades gracefully on ambiguous inputs instead of miscategorizing
Added a session cache to handle multi-step conversation flows in an otherwise stateless bot

title: Cyber Threat Intelligence Platform
problem: Security analysts juggle three separate OSINT dashboards (VirusTotal, PhishTank, Google Safe Browsing) with incompatible data formats and different confidence scoring — slowing triage.
architecture: Designed a GraphQL API on Express.js that normalizes threat verdicts from all three sources into a unified schema stored in MongoDB. Incoming lookups are queued to respect per-source rate limits, and results are cached so repeated queries hit the database instead of burning API quota.
outcome: Single-query threat triage across 3 sources with normalized confidence scores, sub-second cached lookups, and an analyst-friendly UI that presents dense security data without overwhelming users.
keyEngineering: Unified GraphQL schema across 3 external APIs, MongoDB result caching for rate-limit compliance, normalized cross-source confidence scoring.
lessons: Designed a GraphQL schema that reconciles three fundamentally different threat-data models into one queryable type
Implemented a request queue with per-source rate-limit windows and automatic cache fallback
Learned to normalize and compare confidence scores across formats that use percentages, categories, and binary flags
Iterated on UI data density — reduced analyst cognitive load by 2 clicks per triage action
